statement: Phase 1 TP identification in hierarchical search is deterministic given a fixed BLIS seed: all 5 search algorithm seeds select the same TP winner because they evaluate the same BLIS configs at the same seed. Phase 1 failure is therefore total — if Phase 1 fails, it fails on 100% of search seeds. Bracket profiles are also deterministic. This principle is now validated at the full experimental scale: 25/25 (blis_seed x search_seed) combinations on H100 and 5/5 on L40S all confirm identical Phase 1 results per blis_seed.
regime: BLIS with meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct on H100 and L40S, 1000 requests, rate=500, bracket K=1
mechanism: Bracket profiles are derived from parameter range boundaries (max/min of each option list), not RNG. BLIS is deterministic given a fixed --seed. So all search seeds see identical Phase 1 evaluation results for the same blis_seed.
applicability_bounds: Holds for any deterministic profile type (strategic, bracket). Random profiles are search-seed-dependent. For blis_seed-dependent variation, see RP-19.

statement: Bracket Phase 1 profiles (always evaluate max and min of each secondary parameter, max-first ordering) achieve 5/5 Phase 1 correctness on all tested regimes (H100 hard llama, A100 easy llama, A100 hard qwen) while reducing evals_to_best from 7 to 3. Extended in iter-2: bracket K=1 also achieves 5/5 Phase 1 correctness on L40S hard llama (tightest margin tested: 2.1%) and 25/25 across all 5 blis_seeds on H100, confirming hardware and workload portability.
regime: BLIS with llama-3.1-8b-instruct on H100 and L40S, hard regime (1000 req, rate=500), bracket K=1
mechanism: The max profile (mr=512, mt=8192, pf=4096) creates a compute-saturated regime where TP advantage fully expresses at all hardware types tested. The bracket algorithm is hardware-agnostic — it uses parameter range boundaries, not hardware-specific knowledge. Max-first ordering ensures Phase 1 TP winner is determined by the most discriminative profile.
applicability_bounds: Validated on H100, A100-SXM, L40S for llama-3.1-8b hard regime and A100 easy/hard for qwen3-14b. Not yet tested on L40S easy regime or other models. The 2.1% TP margin on L40S is the tightest validated margin.

statement: Bracket K=1 (max-only profile) is sufficient for Phase 1 TP identification and achieves identical evals_to_best=3 to bracket K=2 on H100 hard llama. Extended in iter-2: K=1 also achieves evals_to_best=3 on L40S hard llama (5/5 seeds) and H100 across 5 blis_seeds (25/25 runs). The min profile is universally redundant for Phase 1 correctness.
regime: BLIS with llama-3.1-8b-instruct on H100 and L40S, hard regime (1000 req, rate=500)
mechanism: Since max(mr=512) always scores higher than min(mr=32) at ALL TP levels, the max() per TP is always determined by the max profile. The min profile adds no discriminative power to Phase 1 TP selection. K=1 reduces Phase 1 cost to 4 evals (vs 8 for K=2), freeing 4 additional TPE trials.
applicability_bounds: Holds when the max profile creates compute saturation across all TP levels. If max profile causes OOM or scheduling pathologies for specific TP/instance combinations, K=2 may be needed as fallback.

statement: The min profile (mr=min, mt=min, pf=min) in bracket Phase 1 selects the wrong TP winner. On H100 hard llama, it selects TP=1/8inst. On L40S hard llama, it selects TP=2/4inst. The failure mode is hardware-specific due to different compute-bandwidth tradeoffs. In all cases, Phase 2 TPE within the wrong TP level is trapped, achieving best_score well below the 1% threshold.
regime: BLIS with llama-3.1-8b-instruct on H100 and L40S, hard regime, bracket-min-only
mechanism: At mr=32, the capacity-limited regime dominates. L40S: TP=2/4inst wins (4 instances × mr=32=128 slots) because L40S low bandwidth (0.864 TB/s) makes TP=1 per-request slow, while TP=2 balances capacity and per-request speed. H100: TP=1/8inst wins (8 instances dominate at low batch). On L40S, best Phase 2 score ~0.0917 (16.2% below global best); Phase 2 is trapped in a suboptimal TP subspace.
applicability_bounds: Min profile failure mode depends on hardware. The wrong winner differs between H100 and L40S. In all tested cases, the min profile always selects a non-optimal TP, validating the principle that the max profile is the universal Phase 1 discriminator.

statement: BLIS evaluations complete in ~70-90ms per run on H100 (1000 requests, rate=500) and ~250ms per run on L40S (same workload). Hardware type affects eval wall time: L40S's lower bandwidth creates longer simulation wall times, making L40S experiments ~3x slower than H100. Budget=100 at L40S takes ~25s per search seed.
regime: BLIS with llama-3.1-8b-instruct, 1000 requests, rate=500, H100 and L40S
mechanism: BLIS simulation wall time is proportional to simulated time / hardware speed. L40S's lower TFLOPS (362 vs 989.5) and bandwidth (0.864 vs 3.35 TB/s) result in slower per-request simulation. With 1000 requests at rate=500, L40S takes ~250ms/eval vs H100's ~70-90ms/eval.
applicability_bounds: Scales with num_requests and model complexity. The H100 vs L40S ratio (~3x) reflects primarily the bandwidth difference affecting memory-bandwidth-bound operations.

statement: At a TP margin of 2.1% (L40S hard llama), flat TPE cannot reliably identify the optimal TP level within budget=100: 4/5 search seeds fail to reach the 1% threshold. In contrast, bracket K=1 succeeds deterministically in 3 evals. The relationship between TP margin size and TPE convergence reliability is non-linear: H100 (7.6% margin) shows TPE median evals_to_best=26, while L40S (2.1% margin) shows TPE median evals_to_best=101 (failure). This defines a practical margin threshold below which bracket hierarchical search becomes qualitatively necessary, not just beneficial.
regime: BLIS with llama-3.1-8b-instruct, hard regime (1000 req, rate=500), L40S hardware, budget=100
mechanism: TPE's Bayesian model requires sufficient fitness signal contrast to distinguish TP=4 from TP=8 across the full 10-dimensional search space. At 2.1% margin, the expected contrast is too low for reliable TP=4 identification when secondary params are being simultaneously optimized. TPE may assign high probability to TP=8 configs with favorable secondary params (achieving ~0.108) that appear competitive with TP=4 configs at the same secondary params (0.109), preventing reliable discrimination. Bracket K=1's Phase 1 directly measures both TP=4 and TP=8 at max batch capacity, making the discrimination direct rather than probabilistic.
applicability_bounds: The 2.1% margin threshold is based on a single hardware/model combination. The exact threshold where TPE fails may vary. Margins > 7% (H100) are reliably handled by TPE. The 2.1% L40S margin is reliably handled only by hierarchical search. The transition likely occurs in the 3-6% range.

statement: Bracket K=1 hierarchical search is robust to BLIS workload variation (seed 42-46 on H100): 25/25 (blis_seed × search_seed) combinations achieve Phase 1 correctness and evals_to_best=3. BLIS seed controls workload generation (arrival times, prompt/output lengths) but not the TP-level compute advantage, which is determined by hardware characteristics. The max profile's compute-saturated regime is stable across workload realizations.
regime: BLIS with llama-3.1-8b-instruct on H100, hard regime (1000 req, rate=500), blis_seeds 42-46, bracket K=1
mechanism: The max profile (mr=512, mt=8192) saturates batch capacity at all seeds, ensuring TP ranking is determined by compute efficiency rather than capacity constraints. H100's wide TP=4 margin (7.6-9.5% across all tested seeds) provides substantial safety buffer. Phase 1 TP=4 scores per seed (0.2089-0.2184) all exceed the 1% threshold (0.207103) regardless of workload variation. Seeds 43-46 find actual global bests (0.2113-0.2184) above the seed=42 reference (0.209195), confirming the seed=42 GLOBAL_BEST_TABLE entry is a conservative threshold.
applicability_bounds: Validated for blis_seeds 42-46 on H100 hard llama. Seed robustness has not been directly tested on L40S (blis_seed=42 only in iter-2). L40S's tighter margin (0.85% at seed=44) may be less robust but was not tested via full search.

statement: At 1000 requests/rate=500, flat TPE finds the global best for llama-3.1-8b on H100 within median 26 evaluations. On L40S with tighter TP margins (2.1%), flat TPE fails to converge in 4/5 seeds within budget=100. TPE convergence reliability depends strongly on hardware-specific TP margin: high-margin hardware (H100: 7.6%) is reliably solved, low-margin hardware (L40S: 2.1%) is not.
regime: BLIS with llama-3.1-8b-instruct, hard regime (1000 req, rate=500), H100 and L40S
mechanism: Flat TPE must discover the correct TP level through Bayesian modeling of the full 10-dimensional space. With L40S's tight margin, TPE cannot reliably build a model that distinguishes TP=4 from TP=8 given the noise from secondary parameter variation. The failure is not budget-limited: 4/5 seeds reach best=0.107-0.108 after 100 evals, which is below threshold 0.108571, suggesting TPE is stuck in a TP=8 or mixed subspace.
applicability_bounds: H100 median 26 evals confirmed. L40S median evals_to_best=101 (failure). The transition point is between H100's 7.6% and L40S's 2.1% margin. Adaptive hierarchical search is recommended for all hardware due to the potential for tight margins.
